text.arabic_uthmani: وَكَيْفَ يُحَكِّمُونَكَ وَعِندَهُمُ ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةُ فِيهَا حُكْمُ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّوْنَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ ۚ وَمَآ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ بِٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

words.gloss_range: opening connector that resumes the prior legal scene while launching a fresh rhetorical challenge
words.prose: The opening connector keeps the ayah attached to the preceding arbitration scene (5:42) while starting a new challenge. Its payoff is the boundary movement: the question is not detached commentary, but a connected rebuke that carries the prior legal material forward.

topics.headline: resumptive opening connector
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah opens as a connected challenge flowing out of the arbitration material in 5:42, not as an isolated remark.
topics.reason: The first connector can coordinate or resume, and here it binds the new question to the prior legal scene while preserving a fresh rhetorical frame.

words.gloss_range: rhetorical manner-question that exposes incoherence rather than requesting missing information
words.prose: The manner-question asks how their action can make sense, not whether it happened. Because the ayah immediately supplies the facts that make the action incoherent, the interrogative surface becomes rebuke, and the whole verse unfolds as question, evidence, action, and verdict.

topics.headline: rhetorical how-question
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a rebuking how-question: the wording challenges the coherence of seeking judgment while already possessing the relevant divine ruling.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the word the manner adverb of the arbitration verb, while the following contradiction licenses rhetorical force.

topics.headline: question frames the whole ayah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the verse architecture as a staged challenge, moving from question to evidence to withdrawal to faith-status verdict.
topics.reason: The word opens the operative frame, and later clauses supply the evidence and consequence that answer the challenge.

words.gloss_range: ongoing or characteristic act of making the Prophet the appointed arbiter through the attached object suffix
words.root_gloss_range: judgment, arbitration, restraint, and wise governance; this Form II verb locally selects making someone an arbiter
words.prose: This verb does more than say that they seek a ruling: its Form II shape and attached object make the addressed Prophet the one they try to appoint as arbiter. The judgment root also carries restraining-authority pressure, so the request is for someone to rein in the dispute, while the local form keeps the sense to appointing an arbiter. That delegation is immediately tested against the ruling already located with them, so the judgment root becomes an irony inside the ayah: they try to cause judging while divine judgment is already present.

topics.headline: making the Prophet an arbiter
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the action is delegation: they are making the Prophet the arbiter, not merely asking about law in the abstract.
topics.reason: The Form II verb with the attached second-person object suffix gives the Prophet the direct-object role of appointed arbiter.

topics.headline: restraint image in the judgment root
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels arbitration as restraining authority, while the local form still selects appointing an arbiter rather than every branch of the root.
topics.reason: The root evidence supports restraint and governance pressure, but local grammar keeps the selected sense within Form II arbitration.

topics.headline: requested judgment collides with present ruling
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the judgment language rebound within the ayah: the act of appointing an arbiter is set beside the divine ruling already present.
topics.reason: The same root appears in the arbitration verb and the later ruling noun, and the syntax places possession evidence immediately after the request.

topics.headline: minor sound pressure
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The Form II topic already preserves the forcefulness of the causative verb.
topics.reason: The sound note adds no separate reader-facing payoff after the retained Form II delegation topic.

words.gloss_range: circumstantial possession phrase: while the Torah is with them, in their custody and access
words.prose: This phrase turns possession into the circumstance of the request: they seek arbitration while the relevant scripture is already with them. The suffix keeps the same accused group in view, and the fronted possession phrase makes custody and responsibility the first evidence against the request. That human custody can be contrasted with divine possession formulas elsewhere (6:59, 13:39, 43:85), while the local point remains their responsibility for the Torah.

topics.headline: simultaneous possession as evidence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that their possession of scripture is simultaneous with the arbitration request, making the contradiction immediate.
topics.reason: The phrase is attached as circumstantial evidence to the arbitration verb, so possession modifies the act under rebuke.

topics.headline: custody belongs to the same actors
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the problem is not lack of access; the very actors seeking judgment are custodians of the text that contains it.
topics.reason: The suffix and fronted possession phrase assign custody to the same group involved in seeking judgment.

topics.headline: human custody contrasted with divine possession patterns
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare this human custody with divine possession formulas elsewhere (6:59, 13:39, 43:85), while the local point remains their responsibility for the Torah.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah contrast is useful as apparatus, but it does not override the local circumstantial possession syntax.

words.gloss_range: the recognized Torah as the scripture in their custody and the container of divine ruling
words.prose: The word names a definite, recognized scripture, not an indefinite legal source. Its position makes the Torah the held text around which the contradiction is built: they possess it, and the next phrase says the ruling of God is inside it. The light, concealment, and disclosure pressure lets the scripture feel like a contained source being brought to witness, while the local force remains the foreign proper name as a named scripture.

topics.headline: recognized scripture in their custody
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the critique depends on a named scripture already recognized by the holders, not on a generic book or abstract law.
topics.reason: The noun is a definite foreign proper scripture name and the nominative subject of the possession clause.

topics.headline: light and concealment pressure remains secondary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader may feel the scripture as a contained source of disclosure, while the local grammar keeps the word functioning as a foreign proper name.
topics.reason: The supplied root-image evidence can color the scripture as disclosed content, but the aligned local word is a foreign proper noun rather than an ordinary Arabic root derivation.

topics.headline: Torah contains the ruling named here and expanded next
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a nested authority stack: the group has the Torah, and the Torah contains divine ruling, a thread developed again in 5:44 and 5:46.
topics.reason: The Torah clause is followed by the internal content clause and participates in the nearby legal-scriptural sequence (5:44, 5:46).

words.gloss_range: inside it; a fused preposition and feminine suffix locating the ruling within the Torah
words.prose: This compact phrase makes containment explicit. The feminine suffix points back to the Torah, and the preposition presents the ruling as inside the scripture rather than merely associated with it or derived from it at a distance.

topics.headline: ruling inside the Torah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ruling is located within the scripture itself, so the problem is not absence of accessible authority.
topics.reason: The preposition with the feminine suffix refers back to the Torah and opens the fronted predicate of the embedded nominal clause.

topics.headline: inner layer of the authority stack
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the verse stacking authority: ruling inside scripture, scripture with them, and their request directed outward.
topics.reason: The phrase creates the inner containment layer that answers the preceding legal scene.

words.gloss_range: the singular divine ruling present as stable content inside the Torah
words.root_gloss_range: judgment, ruling, governance, wisdom, and restraint; locally a singular maṣdar in construct naming God's ruling as available content
words.prose: The maṣdar turns judging into available content: the ayah is not narrating a new judgment but naming the ruling already present in the Torah. Its construct with the divine name makes that ruling specified and authoritative, and the singular form lets it read as a unified restraining standard rather than scattered legal detail. The shared judgment root sends the earlier arbitration request back toward the ruling they already have.

topics.headline: specified ruling of God
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees judgment as a stable divine ruling already present, not as an undecided question needing another forum.
topics.reason: The noun is a maṣdar subject in construct with the divine name, making it definite and authoritative.

topics.headline: ruling as restraining standard
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ruling as a unified restraining standard, while the local singular noun keeps the point focused on the divine ruling in the Torah.
topics.reason: Root evidence supports restraint and governance pressure, and the singular construct presents the ruling as a unified authority center.

topics.headline: ruling answers the arbitration verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the judgment root move from their attempt to appoint an arbiter to God's ruling already embedded in scripture, with the sequence continuing in 5:44.
topics.reason: The noun echoes the earlier arbitration verb and prepares the judging-by-revelation language in 5:44.

words.gloss_range: the divine name in genitive, specifying whose ruling is inside the Torah
words.root_gloss_range: divine-name field with worship, turning for refuge, and ultimate authority in traditional derivational discussion; locally the genitive proper name completing the construct
words.prose: The divine name completes the construct and fixes the ruling's source. The issue is therefore not a local community's legal preference but God's own ruling; the name also keeps worship and return-to-refuge pressure near the legal phrase while remaining the construct complement. This is why the later turning away can be read as failed allegiance rather than mere procedural avoidance, a contrast sharpened by the allegiance formula in 5:55.

topics.headline: God named as source of the ruling
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the embedded ruling land on named divine authority, not on a generic or human legal source.
topics.reason: The proper divine name is the genitive second term of the construct and closes the embedded content clause.

topics.headline: worship and refuge pressure in the divine name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the divine name as the authority to whom worship and return belong, while local grammar keeps it as the construct complement.
topics.reason: The derivational pressure is valid background for the divine name, but the local role is genitive completion of the ruling phrase.

topics.headline: God's ruling makes withdrawal an allegiance failure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that turning away from God's ruling connects legal response with allegiance, a contrast sharpened by 5:55.
topics.reason: The ayah places God's ruling before the turning-away verb, and the broader local field contrasts failed withdrawal with allegiance language (5:55).

words.gloss_range: then, with delayed sequence and adversative surprise after evidence has been established
words.prose: The particle is the hinge where available divine ruling turns into condemned withdrawal. It does not merely add the next fact; it orders the rejection as coming after the proof, giving the movement a delayed and incredulous force.

topics.headline: then-and-yet transition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the withdrawal as delayed and surprising: after the ruling has been established, they still turn away.
topics.reason: The sequential particle links the evidence clause to the turning-away clause and carries both temporal delay and censuring surprise.

words.gloss_range: they turn away or withdraw, as an ongoing/reflexive action after the established ruling
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, guardianship, allegiance, and turning away; the local prepositional frame selects withdrawal after access
words.prose: The verb names the action on which the verdict turns. Its Form V shape makes the withdrawal self-involved, and the following after-phrase selects turning away rather than alliance-taking. The root's nearness and allegiance field sharpens the reversal: after approaching judgment and having access to divine ruling, the same group withdraws. The book-judgment refusal pattern is also visible in the close parallel where a party is called to a book for judgment and then turns away (3:23).

topics.headline: same group continues as subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same actors from seeking arbitration into withdrawal, so the final verdict is not shifted onto a new group.
topics.reason: The 3mp imperfect morphology carries the subject without a new noun and preserves continuity with the earlier actors.

topics.headline: withdrawal, not ally-taking
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the root's allegiance field inverted into withdrawal, while the local prepositional frame blocks the ally-taking sense.
topics.reason: The following prepositional after-phrase selects turning away from the prior evidentiary complex rather than taking someone as an ally.

topics.headline: reflexive self-involved withdrawal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels agency in the rejection: they turn themselves away after the ruling is present.
topics.reason: The Form V profile supports self-involved action, and the delayed sequence makes that withdrawal morally charged.

topics.headline: turning-away grounds the faith verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the turning-away verb as the pivot from contradiction to identity verdict, with a recognizable book-judgment refusal pattern also visible in 3:23.
topics.reason: The verb follows the sequence particle, leaves its object recoverable from the prior complex, and leads directly into the final negated believer predicate; 3:23 provides a close refusal parallel.

words.gloss_range: from; origin marker in the compound temporal phrase meaning from after the established point
words.prose: The particle gives the withdrawal a starting boundary. Paired with the following after-word, it makes the rejection begin from a marked point after the evidence rather than float as a vague refusal.

topics.headline: from-after origin point
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the turning away is temporally anchored from after the established evidentiary point, making the refusal retrospective and accountable.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the after-word and forms the temporal origin phrase for the withdrawal.

words.gloss_range: after; the temporal noun that fixes rejection as occurring after the summarized prior matter
words.root_gloss_range: afterness, distance, remoteness, and separation; locally a governed temporal noun in construct with the demonstrative
words.prose: The word makes the withdrawal posterior to a defined point, not just vaguely later. Its construct with the demonstrative makes the after-point specific, while the root's distance pressure colors the refusal as separation after evidence has already arrived. The phrase also sounds like an established after-that refusal formula through the close wording in 2:64.

topics.headline: specific temporal frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the refusal happens after a specific summarized situation, not at an undefined later time.
topics.reason: The noun is governed by the prior preposition and bound in construct with the demonstrative, making the temporal frame definite.

topics.headline: distance colors temporal afterness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels afterness as distancing after evidence, while the local construction keeps the primary sense temporal.
topics.reason: The root supports distance and separation pressure, but the governed construct phrase selects temporal posteriority.

topics.headline: after-that refusal formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the phrase as part of a recognizable refusal formula, especially the close wording in 2:64.
topics.reason: The supplied rows identify the same after-that turning-away pattern in 2:64, which supports a formulaic refusal echo.

words.gloss_range: that; far demonstrative summarizing the prior ruling/request complex as the point after which withdrawal begins
words.prose: The demonstrative compresses the preceding matter into one pointed object of reference. Its masculine singular form resists a Torah-only antecedent and lets the reader keep the ruling, the request, and the whole contradiction in view; its distance also sets the rejected conduct at an evaluative remove.

topics.headline: prior complex compressed into that
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the demonstrative gathers the prior evidence into one threshold after which withdrawal becomes blameworthy.
topics.reason: Reference evidence marks the demonstrative as ambiguous, and the masculine singular form favors the ruling or whole prior situation over a narrow Torah-only reference.

topics.headline: distance in the demonstrative form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels evaluative distance: the preceding conduct is pointed to as that matter before the final denial.
topics.reason: The far demonstrative form carries remoteness while functioning as the construct complement of the after-word.

words.gloss_range: connector that launches the final negated verdict while tying it to the preceding sequence
words.prose: This connector marks the structural threshold into the verdict. It keeps the identity denial tied to the preceding actions while opening a fresh evaluative clause, so the ayah moves from what they did to what they are not.

topics.headline: pivot from narrative to verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final clause as both connected to the conduct and newly framed as an identity verdict.
topics.reason: The connector introduces the final negated nominal clause and creates the transition from action sequence to status judgment.

words.gloss_range: negative particle in the nominal verdict pattern, selecting categorical denial rather than relative or interrogative force
words.prose: The particle opens a nominal negation, not a new action. In the following construction with the reinforced predicate, it denies believer status as a category, so the final clause becomes the ayah's strongest verdict rather than a comment on one imperfect deed.

topics.headline: nominal negation with reinforced predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the final clause is an identity negation, with the particle resolved as negative by the clause architecture.
topics.reason: The following demonstrative subject and reinforced predicate force the negative nominal pattern rather than relative or interrogative readings.

topics.headline: denial of believer category membership
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the negation scopes over their status as believers, not merely over one act in the narrative.
topics.reason: The particle negates the full predicate phrase and changes the verse architecture from question and evidence to verdict.

words.gloss_range: those; plural far demonstrative identifying the accountable group targeted by the final negation
words.root_gloss_range: demonstrative/root background includes pointing, firstness, and return in supplied evidence; locally the plural far demonstrative subject of the verdict
words.prose: The demonstrative points the verdict at the accountable group just described, not at an abstract behavior. Its plural and far-deictic form makes the exclusion corporate and distancing. The supplied root background can only remain secondary, but it lets the pointing feel like a defined group being gathered back for judgment. The following sequence in 5:44, 5:45, and 5:47 turns this pointing form into a local chain of legal-moral verdicts.

topics.headline: accountable group as verdict subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the verdict aimed at the same accountable actors who sought judgment and turned away, not at a vague class of behavior.
topics.reason: The plural far demonstrative functions as the subject of the negated predicate and points back through the referential chain.

topics.headline: firstness and return as background only
topics.reader_payoff: The reader may feel the demonstrative as gathering a defined group back for judgment, while the local function remains deictic subject rather than a lexical firstness claim.
topics.reason: The supplied root field can add background pressure, but the local surface is a demonstrative pronoun in the verdict clause.

topics.headline: forward chain of demonstrative verdicts
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this demonstrative verdict preparing the repeated verdict formulas in 5:44, 5:45, and 5:47.
topics.reason: The same pointing form recurs in the nearby legal-moral verdict sequence (5:44, 5:45, 5:47).

words.gloss_range: as believers; the reinforced negative predicate excluding the pointed group from the recognized believer category
words.root_gloss_range: security, safety, trust, entrusting, and belief; locally the definite Form IV active participle category under emphatic negation
words.prose: The final phrase is the predicate of the negated clause, with the prefixed particle reinforcing the denial. It closes the ayah by excluding the pointed group from the definite believer category; because the root carries trust and security as well as belief, the verdict denies the trust-response demanded by God's ruling. The negative verdict also prepares the stronger labeling sequence in 5:44.

topics.headline: emphatic exclusion from believer category
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the closing phrase as emphatic category exclusion, not as a mild criticism of conduct.
topics.reason: The extra prefixed particle reinforces the negative predicate, and the definite plural active participle names the category from which the group is excluded.

topics.headline: belief carries trust and security pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that denying believer identity also denies the trust-and-security relation that should answer divine judgment, while the local word remains the believer-category predicate.
topics.reason: The root evidence supports faith, trust, and security pressure; the local construction channels that pressure into the denied believer identity.

topics.headline: negative verdict anticipates stronger labels
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah's last word as a negative faith verdict that points forward to the stronger legal-moral label in 5:44.
topics.reason: The final predicate closes the judgment-turning-faith chain and is followed by the next ayah's stronger label (5:44).

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired H-K-M forms in the request to appoint the addressee as judge and in God's judgment, followed by their turning away.
baseline_models.mechanism: H-K-M moves from delegated authority to adjudication: they provisionally hand over the case although an authoritative judgment is already present with them. W-L-Y then makes withdrawal cancel that delegation once it no longer serves them.

activation_trace.role: The delegation and arbitration image makes their request an act of conditionally handing judgment to another.
The adjudication image identifies the Torah's content and the requested act as the same judicial function.
The nearness and presence image removes lack of access as the reason for seeking another ruling.
The withdrawal and aversion image makes their later exit revoke the authority they had just invoked.

changed_reading.before: They inconsistently consult another judge and later reject his ruling.
changed_reading.after: Their consultation is a revocable delegation: they authorize a judge while retaining an exit from judgment.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The Torah is with them and contains God's judgment, yet they create distance after it and are denied the quality of believers.
baseline_models.mechanism: Immediate textual proximity is opposed by enacted relational distance. The closing denial of A-M-N therefore diagnoses the failure of present knowledge to become heart-settled assent, not a mere absence of religious vocabulary or possession.

activation_trace.role: The image of nearness and presence makes the judgment materially and cognitively available.
The distance image turns the temporal aftermath into a relational movement away from what was near.
The aversion image supplies the action by which available judgment is made functionally distant.
The image of assent that settles the heart makes faith the missing internal reception of known judgment.

changed_reading.before: The final clause labels the people as nonbelievers despite their scripture.
changed_reading.after: The final clause defines the failure behaviorally: judgment can be possessed and cited without becoming trusted assent.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier legal inscription is followed by the same temporal hinge and by exceeding the limit. That recurrence turns the focus withdrawal into a patterned post-disclosure breach rather than a single surprising reaction.

activation_trace.role: The image of a secured and well-formed judgment supplies the settled norm from which the sequence departs.
The image of inscription that imposes a judgment supplies an earlier authoritative legal disclosure.
The after-before sequence image supplies the same post-disclosure hinge used in the focus ayah.
The image of crossing a limit gives the earlier sequence its breach outcome.
The withdrawal image realizes the focus ayah's corresponding breach outcome.

structural_cues: 5:32 and 5:43 both move from authoritative disclosure through thumma and min ba'di dhalika to a negative response.
The recurrence occurs within one packet before and at the focus ayah.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated sequence and two different breach verbs; I infer that the repetition marks a durable post-disclosure pattern. A live alternative is that it is only a rhetorical echo.

changed_reading.before: Their turning away is an isolated contradiction after a known judgment.
changed_reading.after: Their turning away instantiates a repeated pattern in which authoritative disclosure is followed by a boundary-breaking response.

context_deltas.mechanism: The legal sequence first presents sanction as deterrence and then allows the aftermath of wrongdoing to move toward repair. Against that route, the focus ayah's movement after judgment goes outward, making withdrawal a refusal of the law's corrective restraint.

activation_trace.role: The prevention and reform image gives judgment a restraining and corrective function.
The exemplary deterrent image supplies law as a boundary meant to stop repetition.
The after-before sequence image opens a contrasting post-wrongdoing trajectory.
The repair-against-corruption image supplies the constructive destination available after wrongdoing.
The aversion image supplies the contrary destination chosen after judgment.

structural_cues: 5:38 presents a sanction as nakal, and 5:39 makes repair possible after wrongdoing.
5:39 and 5:43 both mark an aftermath, but one moves toward repair and the other toward withdrawal.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies deterrence, repair, and the contrasted aftermaths; I infer that the H-K-M prevention branch lets withdrawal reject a corrective process. The alternative is that the legal material is chiefly retributive, not reformative.

changed_reading.after: They refuse the restraining and reparative work that judgment is meant to initiate after wrongdoing.

context_deltas.mechanism: The nearby contrast between spoken belief and absent heart-belief resolves the focus conclusion. Turning away from known judgment is the observable event that exposes speech which never settled into inward assent.

activation_trace.role: The heart-settled assent image defines the quality denied in the focus conclusion.
The assent image spans the explicit contrast between a spoken claim and belief that did not enter the hearts.
The open-mouth speech image supplies the external channel of the belief claim.
The heart image supplies the interior site where the claimed assent is explicitly absent.
The aversion image turns the inner absence into visible judicial behavior.

structural_cues: 5:41 explicitly contrasts saying 'we believe' with hearts that did not believe.
5:43 closes its judicial sequence by denying that the actors are believers.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the mouth-heart contrast and the focus behavior; I infer that withdrawal functions as the behavioral test of assent. A live alternative is that 5:41 and 5:43 address overlapping but not identical subsets.

changed_reading.before: Not-believing is a categorical label appended to their legal inconsistency.
changed_reading.after: Not-believing names the failure of verbal or inherited affiliation to become heart-level trust enacted under an unwanted judgment.

context_deltas.mechanism: The prior instructions disclose a preselected acceptance rule: take a desired result and avoid another. The demand that any judgment be equitable makes the focus referral look like outcome-conditioned forum selection rather than a search for judgment as such.

activation_trace.role: The delegation and arbitration image supplies the forum they provisionally choose.
The image of inclining away from a direction supplies prior manipulation of the governing words.
The taking and possessing image makes acceptance explicitly conditional on receiving the selected result.
The equity image supplies the nonnegotiable standard that frustrates result-shopping.
The withdrawal image becomes the planned response when equitable judgment misses the selected outcome.

surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus verb from W-L-Y, 'they turn away,' after invoking judgment.

strongest_changes: The referral becomes outcome-conditioned delegation rather than sincere submission to judgment.
The Torah's presence becomes entrusted custody within a confirming revelatory chain, not passive possession.

summary.what_was_special: Exact recurrences of judgment, turning, belief, and the post-disclosure sequence made the focus ayah a hinge between legal custody and selective exit; the later W-L-Y field also opened a contained allegiance reading.
remaining_uncertainties: The packet does not settle whether all agents described in 5:41 and 5:43 are exactly coextensive.
The custodial continuity model qualifies the suspicion of referral but does not by itself identify the litigants' motive.
The rein, procedural-cover, and allegiance readings are branch-backed activations that should remain explicitly exploratory.

Eylemden türeyen varlık anlamı, kendisine tapınılan varlığı veya tapınma konusu sayılan nesneyi gösterir.
Ettirgen kullanım, bir varlığı başkalarınca tapınılır duruma getirme veya öyle sunma işlemini bildirir.
Güneşe kimi topluluklarca tapınılması nedeniyle ona tapınılan varlık anlamındaki bir ad verilmesi, varlık anlamının tarihsel bir örneğidir.
